source.title: A Distributed Data-Parallel PyTorch Implementation of the Distributed Shampoo Optimizer for Training Neural Networks At-Scale
source.authors: H. Shi; Tsung-Hsien Lee; Shintaro Iwasaki; Jose Gallego-Posada; Zhi-Jing Li; Kaushik Rangadurai; Dheevatsa Mudigere; Michael G. Rabbat

record.tranche_reason: Compares a different adaptive optimizer, Distributed Shampoo, with SGD using validation performance and training/validation tracking; it does not test the adaptive methods named in V4 directly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports ImageNet ResNet50 training results for Shampoo versus Nesterov SGD, including validation performance and a qualitative comparison of training/validation tracking. The cited optimizer findings in Related Work are not this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares held-out performance of adaptive Shampoo and Nesterov SGD under limited tuning. Its ImageNet results bear on V4, although Shampoo is different from the adaptive optimizers emphasized in the original studies.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors also emphasize that Shampoo matches 90-epoch Nesterov validation accuracy in 60 epochs, reducing total training time by a factor of 1.35. They describe closer training/validation tracking but leave its mechanism unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: Tests Distributed Shampoo, an AdaGrad-family optimizer with SGD grafting, against Nesterov SGD on ImageNet ResNet50; V4 chiefly names Adam and other adaptive methods and discusses broader optimizer benchmarks.
record.method_sensitivity: The training/validation metric disparity between Shampoo and Nesterov is most evident early and is reduced later. The paper also reports Shampoo's validation performance as superior across the tested learning-rate range, while both methods remain sensitive to learning rate.

fits_no_version.finding: Shampoo's training and validation accuracy/loss track more closely than Nesterov's, particularly early in training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer choice affects the training–validation gap during training, with SGD-grafted Shampoo producing closer tracking in this ImageNet ResNet50 experiment.

record.problems: The experiment is limited to ImageNet ResNet50 and compares Shampoo with Nesterov SGD, not Adam or a broad set of adaptive methods. Results use five seeds; the extracted numeric accuracy statement is ambiguous, so the rows preserve the stated qualitative result rather than infer values.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results left out. Performance ablations in Appendix D.2 concern preconditioner frequency and dimension, not the optimizer comparison claim versions.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and chance-level held-out performance compared with natural-label generalization.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width needed to interpolate.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.

Adam and other diagonal adaptive methods; language benchmarks; equal-training-performance comparisons; broader hyperparameter tuning; controlled recovery through decoupled weight decay or switching from Adam to SGD.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove large-batch penalties.
Dropout interventions and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its correlation with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

missing.what: Learning-rate sensitivity comparison: at 90 epochs, Shampoo has better validation accuracy and loss throughout the tested learning-rate range, while both optimizers remain sensitive to learning rate.
Epoch-budget comparison: Shampoo reliably outperforms Nesterov across tested budgets from 40 to 90 epochs. Shampoo at 60 epochs matches the validation accuracy of Nesterov at 90 epochs.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's limits_scope label based solely on untested optimizers and datasets; those are untested parts. The bounded Shampoo reversal does not refute V4's frequency claim across optimizers and benchmarks. Appendix D.2 is explicitly declared in rows_left_out, so it is not listed as missing, although its Nesterov comparisons also corroborate Shampoo's fixed-epoch advantage. Equal-wall-clock comparisons additionally depend on optimizer overhead and training progress.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures on image tasks.
Adam and other named adaptive methods; language benchmarks; broader tuning; AdamW weight decay and switching from Adam to SGD; word-level language models.
Large versus small batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to generalization gaps.
Removal of memorized examples and retraining.

rows.subject: ResNet50 trained with Distributed Shampoo
rows.operation_detail: Train for a fixed budget of 90 epochs using Distributed Shampoo with SGD grafting.
rows.baseline: SGD with Nesterov: better validation accuracy was not observed; see R2.
rows.value: Shampoo consistently achieves better validation accuracy than Nesterov.
rows.uncertainty: Shaded regions show min-max bounds across 5 seeds.
rows.note: The paper reports a qualitative comparison in text; the extracted numeric line is ambiguous, so no value is reconstructed.
rows.check: The state must be relative to V4: Shampoo performs better, reversing the claimed adaptive-method disadvantage. Section 5.2.1 reports mean validation accuracy of 77.44% for Shampoo versus 76.85% for Nesterov across five seeds. Replace the circular baseline with the Nesterov result. Specify SGD grafting, Nesterov momentum, decoupled weight decay, and tuning of preconditioner size and update frequency.

rows.subject: ResNet50 trained with SGD with Nesterov acceleration
rows.operation_detail: Train for a fixed budget of 90 epochs using the Nesterov baseline recipe.
rows.baseline: Distributed Shampoo: consistently better validation accuracy.
rows.value: Nesterov's validation accuracy is lower than Shampoo's in the reported comparison.
rows.uncertainty: Shaded regions show min-max bounds across 5 seeds.
rows.note: The paper states the direction of the comparison; the extracted numeric line is ambiguous, so no value is reconstructed.
rows.check: The direction is correct relative to V4. Mean validation accuracy is 76.85% for Nesterov versus 77.44% for Shampoo. This is the comparator side of R1, not independent evidence.

rows.subject: ResNet50 trained with Distributed Shampoo
rows.operation_detail: Compare training and validation accuracy and loss tracking throughout training.

conditions.value: throughout training; difference most evident early

rows.measure: Qualitative closeness of training and validation accuracy/loss
rows.baseline: Nesterov models show less close tracking between training and validation metrics.
rows.value: Shampoo models' accuracy and loss track each other more closely between training and validation than Nesterov's.
rows.note: This is a qualitative result about the optimizer comparison, not a magnitude-aware sharpness measurement.
rows.check: Closer tracking of training and validation metrics measures the generalization gap qualitatively; by itself it does not establish the held-out performance ordering named in V4. It also does not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness.

rows.subject: ResNet50 trained with SGD with Nesterov acceleration
rows.operation_detail: Compare training and validation accuracy and loss tracking throughout training.

conditions.value: throughout training; difference most evident early

rows.measure: Qualitative closeness of training and validation accuracy/loss
rows.baseline: Distributed Shampoo models show closer tracking.
rows.value: Nesterov models' training and validation metrics track each other less closely than Shampoo's.
rows.note: The disparity is most evident early in training and is reduced later.
rows.check: This duplicates the comparator side of R3. Less close training/validation tracking alone cannot establish V4's adaptive-versus-SGD held-out performance ordering; the original partial state is unsupported.

relationships.condition: ImageNet-1k ResNet50, 90 epochs, SGD-grafted Shampoo versus Nesterov SGD using the Nesterov-tuned training recipe
relationships.reason: R1 and R2 show higher mean validation accuracy for Shampoo, 77.44% versus 76.85%, despite retaining the baseline learning rate, schedule and weight decay; only Shampoo's preconditioner settings were tuned.
relationships.display_finding: Shampoo achieved 77.44% mean validation accuracy versus Nesterov SGD's 76.85%, with only the preconditioner settings tuned.

tranche.reason: Compares a different adaptive optimizer, SGD-grafted Shampoo, against Nesterov SGD on held-out image-classification performance under limited tuning.

source_check.notes: Although extraction interleaves the extrema, Section 5.2.1 identifies the two mean accuracies sufficiently to verify them. The authors also report matching 90-epoch Nesterov accuracy with 60-epoch Shampoo and a 1.35-fold wall-clock speedup; ordinary Adam and its broader tuning are untested.
